title: Enabling vs. directive: How performance management affects innovative performance through thriving at work
content:
by Vincent Goossens, Adelien Decramer, Mieke Audenaert

Rapid changes in the business landscape push organizations to innovate. Scholars, practitioners and policymakers have emphasized the importance of innovative performance to remain competitive. This study investigates how directive and enabling performance management (PM) affect employee innovative performance. Drawing on the socially-embedded model of thriving, we propose thriving at work, the joint experience of vitality and learning, as mediating mechanism. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 461 employees and their supervisors, Structural Equation Modeling results indicate that: (1) enabling PM is positively related to innovative performance through both vitality and learning, whereas for directive PM only learning mediates the negative indirect relationship; (2) both vitality and learning are individually positively associated with innovative performance; and (3) learning only enhances innovative performance when vitality is high. This research explains how distinct PM approaches affect innovative performance and identifies vitality as a critical boundary condition for the learning-innovative performance relationship. These findings suggest that the joint effects of vitality and learning deserve greater attention in future research.
author: Vincent Goossens
